historical_reviews.deepseek: The PARTIAL boundary is sound, but the SSH grep may not survive the intended crash, omits the UEFI/indicator/timing proof and weakens host verification.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Appropriately requires one controlled FAE injection, a bounded outage and recovery/restoration evidence.
historical_reviews.related_cases: IERR denotes a CPU internal-error stimulus; MCERR and UPI timeout/link tests are not interchangeable despite similar catastrophic symptoms.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Critical injection remains operator-controlled with no automatic retry or DUT verdict and complete evidence preservation.

original_test_intent: Inject an Intel internal CPU error into each approved socket and confirm that the platform follows the specified catastrophic crash/reboot path while identifying the affected CPU consistently in OS, BMC, UEFI and physical displays.
original_method: A qualified FAE/operator on an isolated SUT enables the exact EDKII settings, validates the numeric socket against the physical CPU, performs one approved `injectIERR(socket)` call, timestamps the intentional outage independently, waits the authorized autonomous-reboot window, collects IERR/catastrophic evidence after recovery, observes indicators and restores debug settings.
manual_activity: The FAE/operator maps and selects the socket, configures/restores BIOS, triggers the one-shot internal error, observes physical indications and governs the protected recovery timeline. Agent may collect approved evidence only when interfaces are available.
required_inputs: Board/CPU socket map and supported ITP/CScripts package/version/hash
Authoritative IERR/internal-error, BMC catastrophic and UEFI event signatures
Maximum crash/hang and autonomous-reboot intervals with permitted recovery transitions
Front-panel/LCD applicability and correct affected-CPU message
Post-recovery health and BIOS restoration checklist
safety_requirements: Dedicated idle SUT, stable power, independent recovery console and explicit crash approval
Preserve pre-existing logs; do not clear evidence
Verify numeric socket identity before one injection
Do not power-cycle inside the protected reboot window and never automatically retry
Escalate wrong target, thermal/power anomaly, exceeded timeout, no boot or inconsistent evidence
agent_execution_scope: Validate supplied identities and capture non-mutating baseline/post-recovery evidence
Do not change BIOS, run Cscripts, select/inject a socket, reset/power-cycle/retry or decide the DUT outcome
engineer_actions: Approve package, socket map and IERR semantics
Define exact crash/reboot timers, aborts and recovery/restoration
Resolve whether UEFI should record IERR/internal error or UPI fatal and why LCD would show CPU Over Temp
Set deterministic indicator/log acceptance and final verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The proposed remote grep is incomplete post-event evidence, may lose connectivity during the intended outage, cannot prove socket targeting or UEFI/physical/timing criteria and uses unsafe SSH options.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain the FAE-operated `ei.injectIERR(socket)` once the socket mapping and package contract are approved; agent commands remain read-only evidence exports.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Socket 0~N, the explicit socket argument, BIOS paths and 30/10-minute estimates are preserved without choosing a socket or inventing a timeout.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the socket argument to inventory/topology evidence, record full ITP output and an independent outage timeline, correlate BMC/UEFI/OS affected-CPU identity after recovery, capture indicators, restore settings and verify health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds deterministic internal-error identity and bounded recovery while preserving the IERR stimulus.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A generic machine-check grep cannot distinguish IERR from MCERR/UPI faults or prove the requested socket and indicator behavior.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The injected internal error intentionally removes service and may leave the SUT hung, unbootable or with persistent debug/RAS state.

project_override_considerations: Package and operator gates make a controlled future run possible; they do not authorize autonomous crash injection. Missing readiness yields a BLOCKED run, not DUT FAIL.
expected_evidence: Harness hash, mapped socket argument and complete ITP transcript
Independent crash/hang/autonomous-reboot and any manual-recovery timeline
IERR/internal-error OS/console record, BMC catastrophic SEL and corrected recovered UEFI event
Front-panel/LCD affected-CPU evidence, BIOS restoration, health result and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The stimulus is CPU IERR, but Criteria demand a UEFI UPI fatal record and an LCD CPU Over Temp message without defining the platform event mapping. `Reboot eventually` also lacks a timeout and recovery boundary.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The exact internal-error injector and socket parameter make the operation identifiable. Vendor/FAE inputs can resolve signatures, timing and recovery, so this is conditionally executable rather than irreducibly blocked.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 11 Wistron-System RAS-00731-V003: approve CPU socket mapping, Intel ITP/CScripts version/hash and `injectIERR(socket)` semantics; define maximum crash/hang and autonomous-reboot timing, permitted recovery and BIOS restoration; specify exact IERR/internal-error, BMC/UEFI and front-panel evidence; and explain/correct the UPI-fatal UEFI and CPU Over Temp LCD criteria for an IERR stimulus.

review_improvement: The review preserves IERR as a distinct internal-CPU fault and prevents symptoms borrowed from UPI or thermal cases from becoming an unexamined acceptance oracle.
independent_technical_reasoning: The explicit socket parameter makes target validation possible, but only if Intel's logical socket numbering is bound to the physical CPU before halt. IERR, UPI fatal and over-temperature are different event domains; a platform may intentionally translate them, yet the source provides no event-map evidence. During the expected crash the management controller and independent console, not SSH reachability, must anchor timing and fault identity. Because the missing package contract, mapping and timers are obtainable readiness inputs, the safe classification is REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION with execution withheld until the conflicting oracle is approved.
